prior_reproductions: With ORGANON_ROOT set to a private root, a real MCP stdio status call followed root/case/organon.json as a symlink to an external ledger and returned its external item.
A real MCP stdio run call imported an item from that external ledger into the internal case.
Symlinked .organon.lock and .organon.runner.lock let MCP init and run create external files.
Replacing a case or canonical ancestor with an external symlink after the initial path check could redirect the operation.
change: MCP resolves stable aliases to a canonical path under ORGANON_ROOT and opens root and case components by no-follow directory descriptors before invoking the engine through a live Linux procfs fd path.
Ledger and lock files open without following the final symlink, reject nonregular files and stable hardlinks, and do not block on FIFO files.
The installed-wheel crash hook recognizes the canonical parent of the pinned fd path while retaining its exact replacement and SIGKILL controls.
positive_and_negative_controls: A real MCP stdio client still initializes, reads and runs a normal case; an internal symbolic alias to a case and an internal root alias work.
The real client rejects external ledger, initialization-lock and runner-lock symlinks and stable hardlinks without changing the external files.
Deterministic swaps before opening an ancestor are rejected; replacing the name of an already opened case with an external symlink does not redirect the pinned inode.
Invalid init arguments and an enabled ledger anchor do not create nested case directories.

A strict expected-failure test records that relocating the pinned case inode outside the root with the same UID still permits a write there. A future rejection without the outside write becomes XPASS and fails the gate.
Independent review also reproduced a same-UID hardlink race by removing and restoring the external name across fstat. A single st_nlink check is not a continuous exclusivity guarantee.

independent_review.remaining_path_boundary: A directory descriptor pins inode identity, not continuing membership in a mutable root. A concurrent local writer allowed to rename the root, an ancestor or the case can move that inode outside ORGANON_ROOT after it opens. A signed case with an external anchor was also readable after such a relocation; signatures and anchors do not enforce this path boundary.
independent_review.remaining_hardlink_boundary: A local writer able to alter both names can make st_nlink equal one only during fstat, then restore the external hardlink.
independent_review.operational_assumption: The operator controls the root and ancestors and excludes untrusted local writers sharing the server UID; these fd checks are not an OS sandbox.
